key_insight: BrickBench introduces a new way to test whether an AI agent can design LEGO-like structures that are not only semantically on prompt, but also physically buildable. It highlights the need to jointly evaluate creativity, constraint reasoning, and real-world assembly validity.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap in evaluating agentic design systems for text-conditioned LEGO assembly. Existing benchmarks often miss whether generated designs are both aligned with the prompt and physically feasible under discrete part constraints.
method: Defines BrickBench, a benchmark with prompts that require agents to produce valid, buildable brick assemblies from a discrete part library.
Evaluates designs across three settings that vary in scale and part availability to test robustness under different constraints.
Scores outputs on three dimensions: validity, alignment to the text prompt, and overall design quality.
Provides BrickAgent, an environment for coding and testing agentic brick-design solutions.
impact: BrickBench gives researchers a clearer target for building agents that plan under combinatorial and physical constraints. For practitioners, it provides a practical evaluation framework for assessing whether generative design systems can succeed beyond surface-level text matching.
